suggestions.title: Emergency fund in place
suggestions.text: Your cash covers about 4.6 months of essential outgoings, meeting your 3-month target. Keep a small share going to it so it keeps up as your costs rise; anything beyond the target goes to your other choices.

suggestions.title: Higher-rate pension relief
suggestions.text: You pay 40% tax on your top slice of pay, so each £1 into your pension costs you only about 60p. Salary sacrifice also saves National Insurance.
howTo: Ask payroll or HR how to pay more into your workplace pension. Most schemes let you change it at any time.
If they offer salary sacrifice, ask about it: it saves National Insurance as well as tax.
Check your next payslip to see the new amount going in.

suggestions.title: Check for employer matching
suggestions.text: Your employer adds 3%. Many employers add more if you pay more — if yours does, that’s usually the best return available.

suggestions.title: Overpaying the mortgage beats cash savings
suggestions.text: Your mortgage costs 4.2% and cash earns 3.5%, so overpaying is a guaranteed saving once your emergency fund is in place. Investments are assumed to return 4.6% after fees but can fall. Most lenders allow 10% of the balance a year without a charge.
howTo: Check your lender’s yearly overpayment limit first (often 10% of the balance), so you don’t pay an early repayment charge.
Ask whether overpaying shortens your term or lowers your monthly payment.
Set it up with your lender as a regular monthly amount or a lump sum.

suggestions.title: Use your ISA allowances
suggestions.text: You have about £20,000 of your ISA allowance left this year, and Sam has £17,600 (£20,000 each). Growth and interest in an ISA are tax-free. For money you won’t need for at least five years, a stocks & shares ISA has historically beaten cash, but can fall in value.
howTo: Decide between a cash ISA and a stocks & shares ISA (for money you won’t need for at least five years).
Open one, or top up one you already have. The allowance runs from 6 April to 5 April.
Set up a monthly payment on payday so it happens without thinking about it.

suggestions.title: Don’t rush to overpay Sam’s student loan
suggestions.text: On these assumptions it’s written off in April 2044 before Sam repays it, so extra payments would mostly be lost. Your leftover money is likely to do more elsewhere.
